title: Repo size: measuring what is committed and writing the slimming plan

chat.text: .git is 752 MB and public/ is 2 GB, almost all of it the AI sessions store (1.4 GB); the framework code is about 60 MB. An Opus task mastermind measures history by path with a script, decides what should stop being committed, and writes a phased plan (stop the bleeding, archive old sessions, a history rewrite only as your decision). No restructuring in this task.

message.text:
task-mastermind-repo-size-plan: I've finished the repo-size plan and merged it into michael/dev. Screenshots are the problem: they're 84% of git history (397 of 474 MB), while all the session text together is about 30 MB.

### ⚠️ Before the next GitHub push
The next push would send about 160 MB, and about 127 MB of that is screenshots already in commits. Ignoring them now doesn't take them out of commits already made. A history rewrite of only the not-yet-pushed commits would cut the push to about 41 MB (worked out by script).
